scope: Primary and authoritative sources for the frozen 33-chapter, two-volume Komal series. Role-title evidence remains in project-control/roles/llm-engineer/research/evidence-register.json.
method: Prefer original papers, standards/government guidance, official platform documentation, and official open-source documentation. Papers support reported methods/results under their conditions; official docs support current interfaces and implementation examples; neither is treated as universal proof. Volatile implementation facts require edition-time re-verification.

sources.title: Attention Is All You Need
sources.limitations: Foundational architecture paper; predates current model scale, post-training, and serving practice.

sources.title: SentencePiece: A simple and language independent subword tokenizer and detokenizer for Neural Text Processing
sources.limitations: One tokenizer family; behavior depends on the model's actual training tokenizer and template.

sources.title: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units
sources.limitations: Machine-translation setting and early BPE formulation; not a universal tokenizer prescription.

sources.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
sources.limitations: Empirical relationships for studied regimes; later work revised compute-optimal conclusions.

sources.title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
sources.limitations: Pretraining research, not direct evidence for task-specific post-training or product selection.

sources.title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
sources.limitations: One model family and pipeline; human preference is not identical to truth, safety, or task success.

sources.title: Model optimization
sources.limitations: Provider-specific and volatile; use for the evaluate-improve loop, not API permanence.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile
sources.limitations: Voluntary cross-sector guidance; does not prove compliance, safety, or formal approval.

sources.title: Holistic Evaluation of Language Models
sources.limitations: Benchmark scope and models age; task-specific release evidence remains necessary.

sources.title: Working with evals
sources.limitations: Provider-specific evaluation implementation; durable concepts require provider-neutral expression.

sources.title: Define success criteria and build evaluations
sources.limitations: Provider guidance; criteria and methods need consequence-specific validation.

sources.title: Prompt design strategies
sources.limitations: Model-family-specific recommendations and examples change; all require representative evaluation.

sources.title: Structured outputs
sources.limitations: Schema support and subset are API/model dependent; semantic correctness still needs validation.

sources.title: Text generation strategies
sources.limitations: Library behavior and defaults are versioned; strategies do not guarantee task quality.

sources.title: Writing a chat template
sources.limitations: Implementation guide; correct template is model-specific and must match training format.

sources.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
sources.limitations: Findings vary by task and model; later long-context models require fresh testing.
sources.currentness: primary evidence; revalidate on current models

sources.title: More than you've asked for: A Comprehensive Analysis of Novel Prompt Injection Threats to Application-Integrated Large Language Models
sources.limitations: Attack/defense landscape evolves; does not establish universal exploitability or a complete defense.

sources.title: Adversarial Machine Learning: A Taxonomy and Terminology of Attacks and Mitigations
sources.limitations: Taxonomy/guidance, not a guarantee that listed mitigations are sufficient for a specific system.

sources.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
sources.limitations: Original formulation differs from many modern RAG stacks; reported task results do not transfer automatically.

sources.title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
sources.limitations: Open-domain QA benchmarks; production corpora, permissions, freshness, and domain shift differ.

sources.title: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks
sources.limitations: Specific architecture/tasks; embedding quality must be evaluated on the target corpus/query distribution.

sources.title: ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT
sources.limitations: Reported efficiency/effectiveness is implementation and benchmark dependent.

sources.title: Precise Zero-Shot Dense Retrieval without Relevance Labels
sources.limitations: Synthetic hypothetical documents can introduce model assumptions; target evaluation is mandatory.

sources.title: BEIR: A Heterogeneous Benchmark for Zero-shot Evaluation of Information Retrieval Models
sources.limitations: Benchmark diversity is not a substitute for the product's authorized corpus and query distribution.

sources.title: RAGAS: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation
sources.limitations: Automated metrics and evaluator models require calibration; metric labels do not prove ground truth.

sources.title: Citations
sources.limitations: Provider feature and reported internal evaluation; citation correctness still needs task-specific verification.

sources.title: Evaluate a judge model
sources.limitations: Managed preview/implementation details are volatile; human ratings also have limitations.

sources.title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
sources.limitations: Agreement results are judge/task specific; human preference is not universal correctness.

sources.title: G-Eval: NLG Evaluation using GPT-4 with Better Human Alignment
sources.limitations: Evaluated on selected NLG tasks/model; cannot establish evaluator independence or domain authority.

sources.title: RewardBench: Evaluating Reward Models for Language Modeling
sources.limitations: Benchmark coverage and reward-model population are bounded; leaderboard rank is not a release decision.

sources.title: 2024 NIST GenAI Pilot Study: Text-to-Text Evaluation Overview and Results
sources.limitations: Pilot task/report; does not define universal metrics or certification thresholds.

sources.title: Demystifying evals for AI agents
sources.limitations: Agent-oriented guidance and selected internal/customer examples; LLM book uses only transferable evaluation principles.

sources.title: Graders
sources.limitations: Provider implementation; grader correctness and calibration remain the engineer's evidence burden.

sources.title: Dolma: an Open Corpus of Three Trillion Tokens for Language Model Pretraining Research
sources.author_or_org: Soldaini et al. / Allen Institute for AI
sources.limitations: Pretraining corpus at large scale; task-specific post-training recipes need different sampling and rights review.

sources.title: Deduplicating Training Data Makes Language Models Better
sources.limitations: Results are corpus/model/regime dependent; deduplication thresholds create tradeoffs and can remove legitimate repetition.

sources.title: Datasheets for Datasets
sources.limitations: Documentation framework, not proof that a dataset is representative, lawful, or safe.

sources.title: Aya Model: An Instruction Finetuned Open-Access Multilingual Language Model
sources.author_or_org: Üstün et al. / Cohere For AI
sources.limitations: Reported coverage/results do not establish equal capability across languages or transfer to Mosaic's languages/tasks.

sources.title: Self-Instruct: Aligning Language Models with Self-Generated Instructions
sources.limitations: Synthetic generation can reproduce model biases/errors; filtering and independent evaluation are mandatory.

sources.title: Tülu 3: Pushing Frontiers in Open Language Model Post-Training
sources.author_or_org: Lambert et al. / Allen Institute for AI
sources.limitations: One open-model recipe and evaluation suite; methods/results require reproduction for a target base model and task.

sources.title: SFT Trainer
sources.limitations: Library API/defaults are volatile; a trainer cannot validate the data recipe or behavior claim.

sources.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
sources.limitations: Reported parameter/performance results are model/task dependent; later PEFT variants differ.

sources.title: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods
sources.limitations: Implementation catalog; not all methods support all models, layers, quantization, or hotswap paths.

sources.title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
sources.limitations: Hardware, model, optimizer, and evaluation assumptions bound the reported efficiency/quality.

sources.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
sources.limitations: Method assumptions and reported comparisons are task/model dependent; preference data encodes values/biases.

sources.title: DPO Trainer
sources.limitations: Library API and supported combinations change; use only as a versioned lab example.

sources.title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
sources.limitations: Foundational general method; modern generative distillation has additional data, decoding, and evaluation concerns.

sources.title: DistilBERT, a distilled version of BERT
sources.limitations: Encoder-model study, not direct proof for decoder LLM distillation or serving gains.

sources.title: Don't Stop Pretraining: Adapt Language Models to Domains and Tasks
sources.limitations: Pre-generative, encoder-oriented experiments; use to teach the decision, not promise modern LLM gains.

sources.title: Decoupled Weight Decay Regularization
sources.limitations: General optimizer method; training stability and best hyperparameters remain workload specific.

sources.title: FullyShardedDataParallel
sources.limitations: API semantics and recommendations are versioned; generalized distributed infrastructure remains adjacent-role depth.

sources.title: Automatic Mixed Precision
sources.limitations: Operator/hardware support and numerical behavior vary; behavior evaluation remains required.

sources.title: Model Cards for Model Reporting
sources.limitations: Documentation improves transparency but cannot establish fitness, safety, or approval alone.

sources.title: Safetensors
sources.limitations: A serialization format reduces some loading risks; it does not establish artifact provenance or trust by itself.

sources.title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
sources.limitations: Kernel/hardware implementation concerns are adjacent depth; reported speedups depend on workload and platform.

sources.title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
sources.limitations: Reported throughput/latency comparisons are tied to evaluated hardware, models, and systems versions.

sources.title: AWQ: Activation-aware Weight Quantization for LLM Compression and Acceleration
sources.limitations: Accuracy and performance vary by model, task, calibration data, hardware, and runtime implementation.

sources.title: GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for Generative Pre-trained Transformers
sources.limitations: Reported perplexity/speed results do not establish target behavior retention.

sources.title: Accelerating Large Language Model Decoding with Speculative Sampling
sources.limitations: Benefit depends on draft/target model pairing, acceptance, batch/workload, and implementation.

sources.title: Quantization in TensorRT-LLM
sources.limitations: Support matrix and recipes are hardware/runtime-version specific; use only as current implementation evidence.

sources.title: TensorRT-LLM Benchmarking
sources.limitations: Vendor runtime and validated network list; benchmark configuration/hardware must be recorded and behavior replayed separately.

sources.title: Bitsandbytes quantization
sources.limitations: Library/hardware support is volatile; reduced precision requires task behavior and resource measurement.

sources.title: vLLM documentation
sources.limitations: Fast-moving implementation; examples and support must be pinned to a tested version.

sources.title: Latency optimization
sources.limitations: Provider-specific recommendations and cost model; validate end-to-end tails on the target workload.

sources.title: Deprecations
sources.limitations: One provider's current lifecycle; schedules and replacement guidance change.

sources.title: Safety best practices
sources.limitations: Provider guidance and tools do not establish sufficient controls or approval for a specific consequence.

sources.title: Prompt caching
sources.limitations: Provider-specific caching semantics and eligibility; savings depend on request shape and current pricing.

series_claims.statement: Professional LLM engineering owns measured language-model behavior in a system, not isolated fluent samples.
series_claims.limitations: Role accountability is a synthesis; organization topology varies.

series_claims.statement: Tokenization, attention/context, chat templates, and decoding configuration can materially change observable behavior and resource use.
series_claims.limitations: Effects are model/task/configuration specific.

series_claims.statement: Model and access posture should be selected through task evidence plus privacy, control, latency, cost, operability, and change constraints.
series_claims.limitations: No source yields a universal scoring formula.

series_claims.statement: Prompts and messages are versioned interfaces whose changes require controlled, representative experiments.
series_claims.limitations: Prompting guidance changes with model families.

series_claims.statement: Schema-constrained output narrows syntax but does not guarantee semantic correctness, authorization, or safe product effects.
series_claims.limitations: Supported schema subsets and refusal behavior vary.

series_claims.statement: A large context window is capacity, not proof that the model will use every item reliably; position, content, latency, and cost require testing.
series_claims.limitations: Long-context performance changes rapidly across models.

series_claims.statement: Retrieval-grounded generation requires separate and joint evidence for corpus, candidate retrieval, ranking, context assembly, and generated behavior.
series_claims.limitations: Metrics are task- and evaluator-dependent.

series_claims.statement: Provenance, permission, freshness, conflict, and empty-evidence states are distinct from semantic relevance and must survive context assembly.
series_claims.limitations: Implementation controls depend on source systems and authority.

series_claims.statement: Credible LLM evaluation is representative, multidimensional, versioned, segment-aware, and connected to a decision rather than one aggregate score.
series_claims.limitations: Coverage is never complete and thresholds are consequence specific.

series_claims.statement: Model-based graders can scale judgments but exhibit task/model biases and must be calibrated against credible independent judgments.
series_claims.limitations: Human judgments also disagree and may encode bias.

series_claims.statement: Training-data claims require provenance, rights/permission review, quality criteria, mixture, deduplication, contamination controls, splits, and limitations.
series_claims.limitations: Documentation and filtering cannot prove representativeness or lawful use by themselves.

series_claims.statement: Multilingual behavior cannot be inferred from an English average or a model label; language/task segments and tokenizer/data effects need direct evidence.
series_claims.limitations: Aya results do not establish Mosaic performance.

series_claims.statement: Adaptation should begin with a frozen baseline and the smallest intervention whose predicted evidence can falsify the hypothesis.
series_claims.limitations: The intervention ladder is a decision framework, not a universal order.

series_claims.statement: SFT and PEFT can change task behavior with different data, memory, storage, reversibility, and runtime implications; promotion requires target and retention evidence.
series_claims.limitations: Reported gains do not transfer automatically across base models/tasks.

series_claims.statement: Preference optimization learns from a constructed judgment signal and can inherit rater, position, verbosity, style, reward, and grader biases.
series_claims.limitations: Bias form and severity vary by collection, objective, and model.

series_claims.statement: Distillation and continued pretraining serve different hypotheses and carry data, resource, retention, and evaluation burdens distinct from ordinary SFT.
series_claims.limitations: Some cited evidence predates decoder LLM practice and is used for durable principles only.

series_claims.statement: A reproducible post-training claim identifies code, data, split, base model/tokenizer, objective/config, seed, precision, hardware class, checkpoints, evaluators, resources, and limitations.
series_claims.limitations: Exact reproducibility may remain limited by nondeterministic hardware/software and unavailable artifacts.

series_claims.statement: A deployable model-system identity includes base/checkpoint, tokenizer/template, adapter, configuration, schema, evaluator compatibility, runtime, provenance/license, and integrity records.
series_claims.limitations: No single packaging format establishes trust or fitness.

series_claims.statement: Inference choices trade behavior, context, memory, latency tails, throughput, capacity, and cost; benchmark configuration and target behavior must be measured together.
series_claims.limitations: Measured frontiers are workload, hardware, model, runtime, and version specific.

series_claims.statement: Release and model/runtime change require replayable evidence, bounded exposure, observability, rollback, changed-limit recording, and incident learning.
series_claims.limitations: Rollout mechanisms and formal release authority are organization specific.

series_claims.statement: LLM security and safety require layered controls across data, context, model, output, access, artifacts, monitoring, and response; prompt instructions alone are not a sufficient control claim.
series_claims.limitations: No fixed control set is universally sufficient against adaptive threats.

series_claims.statement: Engineers produce technical evidence and recommendations; accountable product, domain, legal, privacy, security, safety, compliance, and organizational owners retain formal decisions.
series_claims.limitations: Exact decision rights must be documented for the organization and use case.
